messages.subject: [Tikzdevice-bugs] A problem on 'sanitize = FALSE' when using pgfSweave
messages.subject_clean: [Tikzdevice-bugs] A problem on 'sanitize = FALSE' when using pgfSweave
messages.body_plain:
Hi smart tikzDevice team,

I've been writing a book on R graphics using pgfSweave and tikzDevice
for several months, and everything works perfect until now: finally I
reached a case in which I have no control of the string containing '%'
in a plot. I could have used sanitize=TRUE in tikz(), but as I'm using
pgfSweave, I wish I can avoid hard-coding like this:

<<fig=FALSE, tikz=FALSE>>=
tikz('some-plot.tikz', sanitize=TRUE)
{plot something}
dev.off()
\input{some-plot.tikz}
@

So I request that 'sanitize' could take values from a global option
like options(sanitize = TRUE/FALSE), or equivalently add an extra
option in pgfSweave named 'sanitize'.

Thanks so much for the great tools!

Regards,
Yihui
--
Yihui Xie <xieyihui at gmail.com>
Phone: 515-294-2465 Web: http://yihui.name
Department of Statistics, Iowa State University
2215 Snedecor Hall, Ames, IA

messages.subject: [Tikzdevice-bugs] My aching sides
messages.body_plain:
Dear writers of tikzDevice,

I have just browsed my way through the source code of tikzDevice, and
it. is. ace. The best-commented source code I've seen in a long, long,
while --- and funny, too! I may even need to make myself a poster out
of it, to keep as an inspiring example.

All the best

Sietse
Sietse Brouwer
Who cracked up when reading the "Mother of all R hacks" commenting in
the tikzDevice.Rnw manual. Still grinning. :-D
